root.label: Non-type template parameters
root.note: Compile-time values that become part of a specialization's identity.

children.label: Allowed types
children.note: The set grew from integers and addresses to floating point and classes.

children.label: C++98 and C++11
children.note: Integral, enumeration, object and function pointers, lvalue references, member pointers, nullptr_t.

children.label: C++20 additions
children.note: Floating-point types and structural literal class types.

children.label: Structural class
children.note: Literal, with all bases and non-static members public, non-mutable and structural.

children.label: Type adjustments
children.note: Arrays and functions decay to pointers and top-level cv is dropped.

children.label: Acceptable arguments
children.note: Each argument must be a converted constant expression of the parameter type.

children.label: No narrowing
children.note: Byte<300> for an unsigned char parameter is ill-formed.

children.label: No int to double
children.note: Floating-integral conversions are not allowed, so Scale<1> fails for a double parameter.

children.label: Class arguments
children.note: A class parameter is copy-initialized, so constexpr converting constructors work.

children.label: Pointers and references
children.note: What an address argument may designate changed in C++17 and C++20.

children.label: Before C++17
children.note: Only the address or name of a complete object or function with linkage.

children.label: Never allowed
children.note: String literals, temporaries, typeid results and __func__.

children.label: Subobjects
children.note: Array elements and members became valid arguments in C++20.

children.label: auto parameters
children.note: C++17 placeholders deduce the parameter type from the argument.

children.label: Type is identity
children.note: X<1> and X<1u> are different specializations.

children.label: decltype(auto)
children.note: Deduces like decltype, so a parenthesized name can give a reference parameter.

children.label: Heterogeneous packs
children.note: template<auto... Vs> can hold values of different types.

children.label: Argument equivalence
children.note: [temp.type] decides when two argument lists name the same specialization.

children.label: Same type required
children.note: Values must have the same type before they are compared.

children.label: Floating point identical
children.note: Identical, not ==, so 0.0 and -0.0 give different specializations.

children.label: Classes member-wise
children.note: Class values are equivalent when their subobjects are, recursively.

children.label: Template parameter objects
children.note: How class-type parameters exist at run time.

children.label: One static object
children.note: A class NTTP names a const object with static storage duration, one per value.

children.label: Scalars are prvalues
children.note: &N is ill-formed for template<int N>.

children.label: fixed_string idiom
children.note: A class holding a char array, deduced by CTAD, carries text as an argument.

children.label: Lambda arguments
children.note: C++20 allows capture-less lambdas as arguments; each lambda is a distinct value.
